source.title: Large Learning Rate Tames Homogeneity: Convergence and Balancing Effect
source.authors: Yu-Qing Wang; Min-Shuo Chen; Tuo Zhao; Molei Tao

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary text are present. The source text has some PDF conversion artifacts in equations and figures, but the relevant prose and theorem statements are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests large-learning-rate GD outcomes in homogeneous matrix factorization, a simplified non-convex setting related to linear networks. It reports convergence and balancing under explicit assumptions, and identifies periodic orbits as another possible outcome; it does not test benchmark classification networks.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's reported scalar and rank-1 matrix factorization outcomes and its general-factorization balancing result. The paper also describes periodic orbits under step size h = 1.9, but reports no training-error measure there; it is not a row for these training-error versions. Introductory claims about other studies are cited prior work and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The scalar-factorization problem is explicitly a two-layer linear network with squared loss and arbitrary hidden width. Its own convergence theory and experiments address V5's recovery above the initial stability threshold, including divergence at larger rates. Balancing alone does not test V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: large constant-step GD can converge beyond the initial 2/L threshold in the proved scalar and isotropic rank-1 cases and induces balancing. General matrix-factorization balancing is conditional on convergence; extension to general deep networks remains future work.
record.recipe_differences: The method is constant-step full-batch GD on squared-loss homogeneous matrix factorization, including scalar and rank-1 cases. It does not use classification networks, benchmark datasets, or the SGD/Adam recipes in V1–V6.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome and guarantees depend on factorization setting, initialization, and learning-rate bounds. In scalar examples, larger learning rates within the stated range produce more balancing; overly large rates may diverge. The supplementary text also reports periodic orbits for a separate step size h = 1.9.

fits_no_version.finding: Large learning rates reduce factor imbalance, including a reported vector-distance decrease from approximately 17.9986 to 0.0154.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large-step GD can substantially reduce factor imbalance in homogeneous matrix factorization.

fits_no_version.finding: GD converges globally for isotropic rank-1 approximation under explicit learning-rate bounds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For isotropic rank-1 matrix approximation, GD converges from almost every initialization under the stated bounds and reaches a balanced minimum.

record.problems: The theory concerns matrix factorization rather than benchmark classification networks. Convergence is proved only for scalar factorization and rank-1 approximation of isotropic A; for arbitrary A, balancing is conditional on convergence. Numerical examples are figure-based, with no reported uncertainty estimates. The paper explicitly notes a substantial gap to deep linear and nonlinear networks.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying result rows were left out. Periodic-orbit examples in Supplementary Section B do not report classification training error or a measure matching the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: CIFAR classification, corrupted labels, convolutional networks, and SGD/Adam training error.
ReLU teacher-student spurious minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and the specified plain/residual network comparisons.
Activation-matched initialization, signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
General nonlinear wide networks; a jointly measured transient loss rise and curvature drop; sustained edge-of-stability hovering; and divergence from below the initial threshold.
Batch-normalization speed and learning-rate comparisons, including Fixup.

missing.what: Scalar-factorization experiments explicitly compare h > 2/L with h < 2/L: above-threshold runs have initially nonmonotonic loss followed by monotone convergence; below-threshold runs decrease monotonically.
For x0 = 20, y0 = 0.07 and µ = 1, loss converges at h = 0.0099009 and diverges at h = 0.01. These rates exceed the approximately 0.005 initial linearized stability threshold.
missing.locator: Appendix E, Figure 17; Hessian formula in Theorem F.2

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Its explicit linear-network formulation makes the scalar results relevant to V5. Section 3 distinguishes its searching phase from the original catapult example by reporting no loss blow-up; Appendix A nevertheless reports initially nonmonotonic loss. This does not establish absence of V5's brief loss rise.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, random or corrupted labels, convolutional networks, SGD or Adam, model size and training duration.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima frequency, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks, depth-dependent classification training error, and normalization or shortcut comparisons.
Activation-matched initialization, signal or gradient propagation, depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and convolutional networks.

Wide-network squared-loss experiments and stability-threshold curvature measurements in the listed original studies. This paper studies matrix-factorization GD at large learning rates, but provides no stability-threshold measurement matching V5.
Batch-normalization comparisons of training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup-trained residual networks.

rows.subject: GD for scalar factorization (3), n = 1, d ∈ N+
rows.operation_detail: Constant-learning-rate gradient descent from almost every initial condition for scalar factorization; theorem guarantees convergence to a global minimum under the stated step-size bound.
rows.measure: Convergence to a global minimum; limiting factor norms satisfy ||x||² + ||y||² ≤ 2/h.
rows.value: GD converges to a global minimum and ||x||² + ||y||² ≤ 2/h.
rows.note: The study's objective is scalar matrix factorization with squared loss, not classification error.
rows.check: The convergence guarantee bears on V5, but does not by itself establish its full loss-and-curvature trajectory. The permitted rate exceeds 2/L near sufficiently unbalanced minima; this is not guaranteed for every initialization satisfying the theorem.

source_check.correct: state: cannot_determine for V5's transient loss-and-curvature trajectory. The stated convergence guarantee and limiting norm bound are correct.
source_check.problem: The row establishes above-threshold convergence and a limiting curvature bound; unmeasured transient behavior does not establish a partially occurring trajectory.

rows.subject: GD for scalar factorization (3), n = 1, d ∈ N+
rows.operation_detail: Large-learning-rate GD from an initially highly unbalanced factor pair; the paper reports the change in the norm gap at convergence.
rows.measure: ||x|| − ||y|| norm gap before and at its limit
rows.note: This is a balancing outcome in scalar factorization, not classification training error.
rows.check: The reported quantity is the vector distance ||x_k − y_k||, not the difference between their norms. The initial norm difference would be 17.91, whereas the reported distance is approximately 17.9986. Balancing alone does not measure any version.

rows.subject: GD for rank-1 approximation of isotropic A (4)
rows.operation_detail: Constant-learning-rate gradient descent from almost every initial condition; the theorem guarantees convergence and bounds the norms at the limiting minimum.
rows.measure: Convergence to global minimum; limiting factor norms satisfy ||x||² + ||y||² ≤ 2/h.
rows.value: GD converges to a global minimum and ||x||² + ||y||² ≤ 2/h.
rows.note: The paper also proves alignment, |cos(∠(xk, yk))| → 1; this is part of the rank-1 matrix-factorization analysis.
rows.check: The learning-rate bound is transcribed incorrectly: its second term is 1/(2√7µ), not 1/(√7µ). The isotropic rank-1 approximation result does not establish the wide-network loss-and-curvature behavior in V5.

rows.subject: GD for general matrix factorization (5)
rows.operation_detail: Stability analysis of GD fixed points; conditional bound on the balancing of a limiting point when GD converges.

conditions.value: GD converges to a point (X, Y)

rows.measure: Factor norm sum and factor difference after the stated SVD rotation
rows.note: This theorem bounds balancing at a converged point; it does not establish convergence for the arbitrary-A general case. The flattened theorem text has damaged equation formatting, so the displayed bound is transcribed cautiously from the readable statement.
rows.check: This is a conditional balancing theorem, not a convergence guarantee or a measurement of the behavior named by a claim version.

relationships.condition: Squared-loss two-layer linear scalar regression, with sufficiently unbalanced initialization and rates within the convergence bound.
relationships.reason: R1 proves global convergence at rates approaching 4/L, above the initial 2/L threshold; Appendix A.1 additionally reports initial nonmonotonic loss followed by convergence, and Appendix E shows divergence at a slightly larger rate. Those experimental results require missing rows.
relationships.display_finding: Global convergence holds at rates approaching 4/L above the initial 2/L threshold, with experiments showing initially nonmonotonic loss before convergence and divergence at a slightly larger rate.
